meta.tagline: Two continents, one Bosphorus: ferry horns, tea steam and eight thousand years of memory

pills: The only city on two continents

overview.title: Welcome to Istanbul
overview.intro: Everyone who tries to fit Istanbul into one sentence loses — the city does not permit it. On one shore, Rome's cisterns and the Ottoman domes; on the other, meyhane songs and third-wave coffee roasters; between them flows the Bosphorus, the most beautiful sea road in the world. The ferry horn, the seagull's cry, the simit seller's call and the call to prayer share the same air. This city is exhausting, crowded — and despite that, perhaps because of it, one of the most longed-for cities on earth. Don't hurry: Istanbul is not a trip but a lifetime project; on this visit, you are only being introduced.

local_word.definition: The untranslatable Istanbul state: an unhurried, purposeless, perfectly calibrated well-being. Tea facing the Bosphorus, wind on the ferry deck, a meyhane table stretching into the night — all are forms of keyif. It is not a plan; it is a consistency.

rules.title: Count the ferry as ritual, not transport
rules.description: The finest road between the shores is the sea: board the ferry, buy your tea, sit on the open deck. Tossing simit to the seagulls is tradition — just be ready for them to snatch it mid-air. Even at rush hour, the ferry is the calmest place in the city.

rules.title: Don't take a step without an Istanbulkart
rules.description: One card works on ferry, metro, tram, Marmaray and bus: buy it at a machine, load it, keep it next to your phone. Transfer discounts apply automatically — the tourist hunting for cash is forever at the ticket booth.

rules.title: Measure distance in hours, not kilometres
rules.description: Istanbul traffic runs on its own laws: at bridge hours, crossing between shores can exceed an hour. Build the plan on the rail + ferry backbone and make the road the last resort — the Marmaray crosses beneath the strait in five minutes.

quick_facts.label: Airports
quick_facts.sub: Both connect to the centre by metro

quick_facts.label: Signature
quick_facts.sub: The sea road between two continents

tip.label: The Istanbul philosophy
tip.text: In this city the plan is flexible and the tea break is fixed: sit down at least twice a day, drink your tea, watch the view. Istanbul is not toured at a run — the ferry you miss at the pier is the view you gain.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: Istanbul's transport has three layers: ferries on the sea, metro and Marmaray beneath the ground, traffic above it. Stay loyal to the first two; use the third like a guest.

items.title: From the airports
items.description: From Istanbul Airport (IST), the metro and Havaist buses run to the centre; from Sabiha Gökçen (SAW), the metro connects to Kadıköy. Both journeys approach an hour — in Istanbul, airport distance is taken seriously.

items.title: The ferries — the city's backbone
items.description: The Şehir Hatları ferries shuttle between Eminönü, Karaköy, Beşiktaş, Kadıköy and Üsküdar: this is the most beautiful 'metro line' there is. A tea galley on board, seagulls in pursuit — the 20-minute crossings are the city's cheapest Bosphorus cruise.

items.title: The metro and the Marmaray
items.description: The metro network has grown fast; the Marmaray links two continents in five minutes through a tube beneath the strait. The Sirkeci-Üsküdar crossing is an engineering marvel folded into daily life.

items.title: The T1 tram and the nostalgic lines
items.description: The T1 runs the length of the historic peninsula from Kabataş to Sultanahmet: the visitor's main artery. İstiklal's red nostalgic tram and the Tünel — the world's second-oldest metro — are short but sweet classics.

items.title: Taxis and dolmuş — use knowingly
items.description: Call taxis by app and watch the meter; over short distances the rails almost always win. The dolmuş — the city's own shared taxi — is practical for those who know its routes.

callout.label: Ferry tip
callout.text: In the late afternoon board the Karaköy-Kadıköy ferry and sit on the left: at sunset the historic peninsula's silhouette — domes and minarets — is drawn against an orange sky. The city's best view costs one tap of an Istanbulkart.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Istanbul choosing a district is choosing a city: the domes of the historic peninsula, Galata's art, Cihangir's bohemia, Kadıköy's local rhythm.

local_word.definition: Istanbul's true unit: a small self-sufficient universe with its grocer, bakery, coffeehouse and headman. The answer to 'which district' is not a hotel but which mahalle's morning you want to wake into.

items.name: Sultanahmet
items.description: Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque and Topkapı within walking distance: the classic base for a first visit. It quietens at night and its restaurants are tuned to tourists — ideal for the history dose, not for nightlife.

items.name: Galata and Karaköy
items.description: Boutique hotels, galleries and third-wave coffee in the tower's shadow: the best blend of history and new life. Ferries link it to both shores — the city's balanced base camp.

items.name: Cihangir and Beyoğlu
items.description: Antique dealers, cat-filled cafés and Bosphorus-view slopes: Istanbul's artists' quarter. İstiklal's energy is two streets away, the mahalle's calm within.

items.name: Kadıköy and Moda
items.description: The heart of the Asian side: its market, its meyhanes, its seaside walk and everyday Istanbul life. Off the tourist route, yet twenty minutes from everywhere by ferry — for those who tour by living.

items.name: The Beşiktaş–Ortaköy line
items.description: A lively market, a busy pier, a long shoreline: the address of life beside the Bosphorus. The breakfast streets and match days give the quarter a rhythm of its own.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Istanbul's four seasons are four different cities: Judas-tree purple in spring, Bosphorus evenings in summer, bluefish in autumn, and — with luck — snow-covered domes in winter.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Judas Tree Season
items.subtitle: Spring · The tulip festival, purple Bosphorus hills
items.description: In April the parks fill with tulips, and at April's end the Bosphorus hills turn Judas-tree purple — the city's shortest, most legendary season. The weather is made for walking, the terraces open, the islands green.

callout.label: Judas tree tip
callout.text: In late April or early May take a ferry up the Bosphorus: the slopes of Kuzguncuk, Kandilli and Emirgan are painted purple. The erguvan lasts two weeks — if you coincide, cancel every plan and get out on the water.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Bosphorus Evenings
items.subtitle: Summer · Hot humid days, long seaside nights
items.description: The daytime heat and humidity are tiring; the city returns to life with the evening cool — the shores fill, the meyhane tables spill into the streets, the islands open their sea season. Plan for morning and evening; give midday to the museums.

callout.label: August note
callout.text: Don't go to the Princes' Islands at the weekend: ferries and shores overflow. Take a weekday morning boat, rent a bicycle and pedal the pine ridges — the island shows its true face on its quiet days.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Bluefish and Golden Light
items.subtitle: Autumn · The most balanced season, fish season
items.description: September-October is Istanbul at its best: soft air, golden light, a sea still warm. The lüfer (bluefish) season opens on the Bosphorus, the meyhane tables grow richer, and in Biennial years the city drowns in art.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: In October give one evening to a Bosphorus-side meyhane and ask for lüfer: in its season, bluefish is the crown of the Istanbul table. Rakı beside it, the sea before you — autumn's official menu.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Chance of Snowy Domes
items.subtitle: Winter · Rainy days, sahlep and museum season
items.description: Winter is rainy and grey, but it suits the city: museums calm, tea houses full, the sahlep sellers at work. If it snows, drop everything — Hagia Sophia and Süleymaniye under snow are Istanbul's rarest postcard.

callout.label: Snow-day tip
callout.text: On the day snow falls, climb to the Süleymaniye courtyard: the domes turn white, the Golden Horn vanishes into mist, and the city becomes an Ottoman miniature. It happens rarely — and when it does, even the city stops to watch.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Istanbul table is an imperial inheritance: the tradesman's lokanta pot, the meyhane's meze, the street's simit and the baklava's syrup all live in one day.

local_word.definition: The small-plated army of the meyhane table: fava, ezme, topik, lakerda... The aim is not to fill up but to stretch the table. Meze is rakı's travelling companion and conversation's excuse — the more plates arrive, the longer the night.

items.name: The esnaf lokantası pot
items.description: White beans over rice, stuffed aubergine, meatballs in broth: choose by pointing at the pots behind the glass. Süleymaniye's historic bean houses and the neighbourhood lokantas are the heart of the city's everyday cooking.
items.tag: Lunch classic · point at the pot

items.name: The meyhane ritual — rakı and meze
items.description: Start with cold meze, continue with hot starters, crown it with fish: rakı is drunk slowly and the table lasts for hours. From Nevizade to Kadıköy, every meyhane has its regulars and its story.

items.name: Simit, tea and breakfast culture
items.description: The morning simit is bought fresh and crackling, the tea drunk from a tulip glass; at weekends the spread breakfast takes over whole tables. Tea + simit on the ferry deck is Istanbul's cheapest formula for happiness.
items.tag: Morning ritual · valid on the ferry too

items.name: The köfte and döner classics
items.description: Grilled köfte with bean salad at the historic köfte houses, döner carved by a master's hand: the summit of things that look simple. The shop with the queue is usually the right shop.
items.tag: From a master · a queue is a good sign

items.name: Fish sandwiches and stuffed mussels
items.description: Eminönü's balık ekmek is a contested classic; the midye dolma of the side streets a late-night legend: squeeze the lemon, count the shells later. This is the street food of a sea city.
items.tag: Street classic · with plenty of lemon

items.name: The baklava + Turkish coffee finale
items.description: Pistachio baklava from a master, coffee brewed on embers and served with its grounds: the table's constitutional close. Reading the coffee cup is not science but the art of conversation — turn the cup over and wait.
items.tag: Sweet finale · the fortune is a bonus

callout.label: The lokanta rule
callout.text: Three signs of the right place in Istanbul: an esnaf lokantası full at noon, a handwritten menu in the window, and a local crowd at the tables. Two streets behind any tourist square is almost always both better and cheaper.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone sees Hagia Sophia; these six are the Istanbul that hides itself mahalle by mahalle.

items.name: Kuzguncuk
items.description: Coloured wooden houses, a centuries-old plane tree, and a mosque, church and synagogue standing side by side: the Bosphorus's most graceful mahalle. Tomatoes grow in its market garden and time slows in its cafés — Istanbul's 'if only it were always like this' state.

items.name: Balat and Fener in the morning
items.description: Steep lanes, bay-windowed houses, the Greek Patriarchate and antique shop windows: the old world of the Golden Horn. Go early — as the breakfast places open, the streets are yours before the photographers.

items.name: The Süleymaniye courtyard and Golden Horn view
items.description: The complex Sinan called 'my journeyman work' holds the city's most serene courtyard and its most generous Golden Horn terrace: at sunset the whole silhouette, from Galata Tower to the Bosphorus, lies at your feet.

items.rarity: The street where a novel became a museum
items.name: Çukurcuma and the Museum of Innocence
items.description: In the middle of the antique dealers' quarter stands the museum born from Orhan Pamuk's novel: the only place on earth where fiction turned into objects. The junk-shop windows of the surrounding streets are the museum's natural continuation.

items.name: The pine ridges of the Princes' Islands
items.description: The motor-free roads of Büyükada and Heybeliada are toured by bicycle: mansions, pine scent and paths dropping to the sea. Go on a weekday morning ferry — on its quiet days the island is another century.

items.name: Kariye (Chora)
items.description: This old Byzantine building near the land walls carries some of the world's most moving mosaics and frescoes: intricate stories on gold ground. A quiet, deep alternative to Hagia Sophia's crowds.

callout.label: Bosphorus tip
callout.text: Instead of a tourist cruise, use the Şehir Hatları long Bosphorus run or the ordinary Üsküdar-Beşiktaş line: the same sea, the same waterfront mansions, at Istanbulkart prices. Get off at Kuzguncuk on the way back — the tea garden is the route's reward.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Istanbul is hospitable, but the classic games run in the tourist core; know these four and wander easy.

items.name: The tout and the priceless menu
items.description: At some restaurants on the tourist squares, the door-tout and the unpriced 'fish of the day' end in a surprise bill.
items.instead: Order nothing without a written price; enter where the locals sit, not where the doorman pulls. The two-streets-back rule is worth gold in this city.

items.name: Meter and route games
items.description: Some taxis 'forget' the meter, take the long way round, or perform sleight of hand with the change on a large note.
items.instead: Call the taxi by app, follow the route on your map, break the big note before boarding. Over short distances the rails + ferry are cheaper and faster anyway.

items.name: Saying yes to the Grand Bazaar's first price
items.description: The bazaar's first price is an opening line, and the 'gift tea + carpet showing' chain is a classic sales choreography.
items.instead: Haggle with a smile and at ease, and don't settle in over something you won't buy. The tea offering is a lovely tradition — accept it without feeling indebted; 'thank you, just looking' suffices.

items.name: The 'friendly' night invitation
items.description: At the bar suggested by a newly met 'friend' in the tourist quarter, the bill arrives astronomical, and objections meet security at the door.
items.instead: Choose your own night venue and never change it on an invitation. Real Istanbul conversation lives in the meyhane, the tea house and the mahalle coffeehouse — there both the bill and the talk are honest.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: Smile and keep walking past anyone who blocks your path to sell you something; sit down and talk with the mahalle tradesman who offers you tea. The day you learn to tell the two apart, the city opens its doors to you.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From domes to ferry, from empire to meyhane

steps.title: Sultanahmet Square, early
steps.description: Stand between Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque before the crowds: watch a fifteen-hundred-year confrontation in morning light. Enter Hagia Sophia at opening.

steps.title: The Basilica Cistern and the Grand Bazaar
steps.description: Cool off in the cistern's columned dusk, then lose yourself in the bazaar's streets: haggling allowed, hurrying forbidden.

steps.title: A Süleymaniye noon
steps.description: White beans over rice at a historic bean house, then Sinan's courtyard and the Golden Horn terrace: Istanbul's finest lunch-break combination.

steps.title: Change continents by ferry
steps.description: Board the Kadıköy ferry at Eminönü: tea + simit + seagulls. Across the water, walk the market and the Moda seafront — join the city's local rhythm.

steps.title: A Galata sunset
steps.description: Ferry back to Karaköy and climb the slopes towards the tower: at sunset the rooftops and the Golden Horn turn crimson. A coffee break on Serdar-ı Ekrem street.

steps.title: A meyhane night
steps.description: A meyhane table in Beyoğlu or Kadıköy: cold meze, rakı and conversation that stretches. An Istanbul day closes at the table, with a 'şerefe'.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: The peninsula, the Bosphorus and the mahalles — three Istanbuls

steps.title: Classic Istanbul
steps.description: The one-day flow above: Sultanahmet, the bazaar, Süleymaniye, the ferry, Galata, the meyhane.

steps.title: Bosphorus day
steps.description: Topkapı Palace and the harem in the morning; the Bosphorus line by ferry in the afternoon — a kumpir stop at Ortaköy, tea at Kuzguncuk via Üsküdar; fish by the water at night, lüfer if in season.

steps.title: Mahalles and farewell
steps.description: The Balat-Fener lanes and the Kariye mosaics in the morning; Çukurcuma's antique shops + the Museum of Innocence in the afternoon — or, on a weekday, an island escape; the farewell close is Turkish coffee and a fortune reading — cup overturned, heart open.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Istanbul's daily language is warm; these five words open every door in the city.

items.meaning: Hello — with a smile, it opens every door
Thank you — the casual form is 'sağ ol'
'Welcome, come in, what would you like' — the shopkeeper's word of invitation; heard fifty times a day
Said to anyone at work: 'may it come easy' — the city's invisible greeting
Cheers! — at the rakı table, eye contact and conversation are mandatory

checklist.title: Istanbul Checklist
checklist.completion_message: Şerefe! You've lived both continents properly!

items.label: Drink tea on the ferry, toss simit to the gulls
Stand beneath Hagia Sophia's dome
items.sub: At opening — fifteen centuries above you

items.label: Look over the Golden Horn from Süleymaniye
Set a rakı-meze table at a meyhane
items.sub: No hurry — the table lasts for hours

items.label: Haggle in the Grand Bazaar
items.sub: With a smile, tea offering included

items.label: Walk Balat's coloured lanes in the morning
Drink coffee under Kuzguncuk's plane tree
items.sub: Mosque, church and synagogue side by side

items.label: Cross beneath the strait on the Marmaray
Drink Turkish coffee, have your cup read
